==English== {{wp|}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ɡeɪm/|a2=<>|[ɡeɪ̯m]|a3=<>|[ɡɛi̯m]}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-game.ogg|a=US|IPA=[ɡ̊ẽːm]}} * {{IPA|en|/ɡæɪm/|[ɡæ̝ɪ̯m]|a=AU,NZ}} * {{rhymes|en|eɪm|s=1}} * {{hyph|en|game}} ===Etymology 1=== {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:game|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|game}}, {{m|enm|gamen}}, {{m|enm|gammen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|gamen||sport, joy, mirth, pastime, game, amusement, pleasure}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*gaman}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*gamaną||amusement, pleasure, game", literally "participation, communion, people together}}, from {{m|gem-pro|*ga-|pos=collective prefix}} + {{m|gem-pro|*mann-||man}}; or alternatively from {{m|gem-pro|*ga-}} + a root from {{der|en|ine-pro|*men-||to think, have in mind}}. Cognate with {{cog|yol|gaame}}, {{m|yol|gaaume}}, {{m|yol|gaume||game}}, {{cog|ofs|game}}, {{m|ofs|gome|t=joy, amusement, entertainment}}, {{cog|nl|gemelijk|t=cantankerous, crabbed}}, {{cog|gmh|gamen|t=joy, amusement, fun, pleasure}}, {{cog|da|gammen|t=merriment}}, {{cog|is|-}}, {{cog|nn|gaman|t=joy, fun}}, {{cog|sv|gamman|t=mirth, rejoicing, merriment}}. Related to {{l|en|gammon}}, {{l|en|gamble}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun|~}} # {{senseid|en|any playful or competitive activity}} A [[playful]] or [[competitive]] [[activity]]. ## {{senseid|en|any playful amusement or pastime}} A playful activity that may be unstructured; an [[amusement]] or [[pastime]]. ##: {{syn|en|amusement|diversion|entertainment|festivity|frolic|fun|gaiety|gambol|lark|merriment|merrymaking|pastime|play|prank|recreation|sport|spree}} ##: {{ant|en|drudgery|work|toil}} ##: {{ux|en|Being a child is all fun and '''games'''.}} ## {{lb|en|countable}} An activity described by a set of [[rule]]s, especially for the purpose of [[entertainment]], often [[competitive]] or having an explicit [[goal]]. ##: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:game}} ##: {{ux|en|'''Games''' in the classroom can make learning fun.}} ##* {{quote-av|en|year=1983|writers=w:Lawrence Lasker; et al.|title=w:WarGames|passage=''Joshua:'' Shall we play a '''game'''?
''David:'' ... Love to. How about Global Thermonuclear War?
''Joshua:'' Wouldn't you prefer a good '''game''' of chess?
''David:'' Later. Let's play Global Thermonuclear War.
''Joshua:'' Fine.}} ## {{lb|en|UK|in plural}} A school subject during which [[sport]]s are practised. ##* {{RQ:Fry Liar|page=26|passage=From time to time tracksuited boys ran past them, with all the deadly purpose and humourless concentration of those who enjoyed '''Games'''.}} ## {{senseid|en|any particular instance or match of gameplaying}} {{lb|en|countable}} A particular instance of playing a game. ##: {{syn|en|match}} ##: {{ux|en|Sally won the '''game'''.}} ##: {{ux|en|They can turn the '''game''' around in the second half.}} ##* {{RQ:Ferguson Zollenstein|I|passage=“I'm through with all pawn-games,” I laughed. “Come, let us have a '''game''' of lansquenet. Either I will take a farewell fall out of you or you will have your sevenfold revenge”.}} ## {{lb|en|tennis}} Part of a [[set]] during which one player continuously [[serves]] (at least four [[rallies]] must be won to win a game, at least six games must be won to win the set). ##: {{ux|en|'''Game''', set and match!}} ## {{senseid|en|the stakes that are at stake}} That which is gained, such as the [[stake]] in a game. ## {{senseid|en|number of points constituting a win}} The number of [[point]]s necessary to win a game. ##: {{ux|en|In [[short whist]], five points are '''game''', while in in [[table tennis]] '''game''' is 21 points.}} ##: See also: {{l|en|for the win}} ## {{senseid|en|bonus point for highest hand}} {{lb|en|card games}} In some games, a [[point]] awarded to the [[player]] whose [[card]]s add up to the largest [[sum]]. ## {{senseid|en|any particular instance of the physical equipment or software for playing a specific game}} {{lb|en|countable}} The equipment that enables such activity, particularly as packaged under a title. ##: {{ux|en|Some of the '''games''' in the closet we have on the computer as well.}} ## {{senseid|en|one's gameplaying manner}} One's manner, style, or performance in playing a game. ##: {{ux|en|Study can help your '''game''' of chess.}} ##: {{ux|en|Hit the gym if you want to toughen up your '''game'''.}} ##* {{RQ:Salinger Catcher|chapter=11|passage=I played golf with her that same afternoon. She lost eight balls, I remember. Eight. I had a terrible time getting her to at least open her eyes when she took a swing at the ball. I improved her '''game''' immensely, though.}} ## {{senseid|en|video game}} {{lb|en|countable}} {{ellipsis of|en|video game}}. ##* {{RQ:Guardian|date=May 8 2019|title=Save yourself! The video games casting us as helpless children|author=Jon Bailes|passage=There’s a sense here, as well as in '''games''' such as Limbo, that we’re making ourselves experience our children’s reality, trapped in the chaos that the adults have created.|url=https://www.theguardian.com/games/2019/may/08/video-games-casting-adults-as-helpless-children-last-guardian|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261013162057/https://www.theguardian.com/games/2019/may/08/video-games-casting-adults-as-helpless-children-last-guardian|archivedate=13 October 2026}} # {{senseid|en|an industry or business line}} {{lb|en|countable|usually|in the singular|informal}} A field of gainful activity, as an [[industry]] or [[profession]]. #: {{syn|en|line}} #: {{ux|en|When it comes to making sales, John is the best in the '''game'''.}} #: {{ux|en|He's in the securities '''game''' somehow.}} ## {{lb|en|[[hip-hop]]|with ''the''}} The music industry. ##: {{ux|en|The [[rapper]] bragged about how he ran '''the game'''.}} # {{senseid|en|any system with rules comparable to a designed competition}} {{lb|en|countable|figuratively}} Something that resembles a game with rules, despite not being designed. #: {{ux|en|In the '''game''' of life, you may find yourself playing the waiting '''game''' far too often.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 5|page=77|act=II|scene=i|column=2|passage=I ſee you ſtand like Grey-hounds in the ſlips, / Straying vpon the Start. The '''Game'''’s afoot:}} #* {{RQ:Ferguson Zollenstein|I|passage=“I'm through with all pawn-'''games''',” I laughed. “Come, let us have a game of lansquenet. Either I will take a farewell fall out of you or you will have your sevenfold revenge”.}} # {{senseid|en|war simulation}} {{lb|en|countable|military}} An exercise [[simulating]] [[warfare]], whether computerized or involving human participants. #: {{syn|en|wargame}} # {{senseid|en|unethical practice}} {{lb|en|countable}} A questionable or unethical practice in pursuit of a goal. #: {{syn|en|scheme|racket}} #: {{ux|en|You want to borrow my credit card for a week? What's your '''game'''?}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1902|title=Dryden|author=w:George Saintsbury|page=182|passage=It was obviously Lord Macaulay's '''game''' to blacken the greatest literary champion of the cause he had set himself to attack.}} # {{senseid|en|wild animals hunted for food}} {{lb|en|uncountable}} [[wild animal|Wild animals]] hunted for food. #: {{ux|en|The forest has plenty of '''game'''.}} # A [[flock]] of [[swan]]s, especially as kept for hunting purposes (or, originally, a group of any animals kept for such purpose). #*{{RQ:Joyce Portrait|chapter=V||A '''game''' of swans flew there and the water and the shore beneath were fouled with their greenwhite slime.}} # {{senseid|en|seduction effort}} {{lb|en|uncountable|informal|used mostly for men}} The ability to [[seduce]] or [[woo]] someone, usually by strategy. #: {{syn|en|rizz}} #: {{ux|en|He didn't get anywhere with her because he had no '''game'''.}} # {{senseid|en|flirtation}} {{lb|en|now|rare}} [[lovemaking|Lovemaking]], [[flirtation]]. # {{senseid|en|sex work}} {{lb|en|slang}} {{U|prostitution}}. (Now chiefly in {{m|en|on the game}}.) #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Troilus and Cressida|act=IV|scene=v|lines=61–63|page=617|passage=ſet them downe, / For ſlottiſh ſpoyles of opportunitie; / And daughters of the '''game'''.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1755|translator=w:Tobias Smollett|author=Miguel de Cervantes|title=Don Quixote|section=Volume 1, I.2 |passage=[H]e put spurs to his horse, and just in the twilight reached the gate, where, at that time, there happened to be two ladies of the '''game''' {{transterm|es|[[mujer|mugeres]] [[moza|moças]]}}, who being on their journey to Seville, with the carriers, had chanced to take up their night's lodging in this place.}} # {{senseid|en|mastery}} {{lb|en|uncountable|slang}} [[mastery|Mastery]]; the ability to [[excel]] at something. # {{lb|en|uncountable|archaic}} [[diversion#Noun|Diversion]], [[entertainment#Noun|entertainment]]. #* {{RQ:Hall Epistles|volume=III|epistle=VIII|chapter=To E.B. Dedicated to Sir George Goring|pages=95–96|pageref=95|passage=To ſet the minde on the racke of long meditation (you ſay) is a torment: to follow the ſwift foote of your hound alday long, hath no wearineſſe: what would you ſay of him that finds better '''game''' in his ſtudie, then you in the fielde, and would account your diſport his puniſhment? ſuch there are, though you doubt and wonder.}}
